external_content_policy: API/page text treated as untrusted data; no instructions in retrieved content were executed; no CAPTCHA/Anubis/Cloudflare challenge was bypassed and no credentials were used.
goal: Probe academic/archive surfaces for ReactOS compatibility research; record the cheapest suitable tool per family, real status and zero-result lanes.
tool_selection: Direct HTTP JSON/XML APIs first (stdlib urllib in the isolated research environment; curl only as a single alternative client after a client-side TLS failure). Browser automation was not used: no API lane required JS, and challenge pages were stopped rather than solved.
uncertainty: Search APIs rank by relevance and may return substring false positives ("REACTOS" as plural of reactor, "REACTO" as a different project); relevance was judged from returned titles, not from API totals.

tool_selection_reason: Single JSON request; browser unnecessary and more expensive; cheapest suitable tool for a REST API.
uncertainty: Large API totals are corpus-wide fuzzy matches, not ReactOS hits; no DOI-level screening beyond returned titles was performed.

conclusion: Six academic/archive surfaces were probed with the cheapest suitable tool per family. Three returned data (Crossref, arXiv, OpenAlex); three were blocked or throttled and are reported as no-evidence lanes. No peer-reviewed ReactOS compatibility study was found in the successful lanes; the only title-matched item is a 2006 Spanish magazine article in OpenAlex.
uncertainty: API relevance ranking and title-only screening can miss papers indexed under other terms; blocked lanes are not proof of absence.
